conviction_note: The findings sum to -4.5. The scaled number is -2.2 (p_up 42, abs 14). The weight sits on the FY guide arithmetic from company documents. H1 revenue was $43.9m against a $99-103m guide, so Q4 has to reach about $29-33m. The 10-Q says HEMOBLAST supply after Q3 is uncertain, so a guide cut looks likely. Two-analyst consensus still sits near the old guide. Three things keep p_up near 50: the stock is already at its 52-week low, down 41% since the August print; the Q3 revenue bar is disputed between sources; and the HEMOBLAST switch to gross revenue could make Q3 look like a sequential beat. The gap between the two numbers is that p_up uncertainty. It does not mean the findings are wrong.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is disputed. Benzinga's English page shows $25.5m and its Korean page $27.1m; StockAlarm shows about $27m from 2 analysts (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XTNT/earnings-forecasts, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/XTNT/earnings-forecasts, https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/XTNT/analysts). EPS consensus is about -$0.01 to -$0.02. The FY2026 company guide of $99-103m, cut from $101-105m on 2026-08-11 (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/XTNT/xtant-medical-reports-q2-2026-financial-results), is the sourced bar. Street FY consensus is about $102m and Q4 about $30.1m, i.e. not reset below the guide. Because the quarterly bar is disputed, findings that depend on it are capped small. The guide finding rests on the company's own range.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 375k shares, roughly 0.3% of the ~140.3m shares outstanding, with 3.86 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, https://equibles.com/stocks/xtnt/shortinterest). That is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism against a negative. There is no options market, so no skew. Spot is $0.264, a 52-week low, -67% from the 52-week high, -8.97% over 5 and 20 days, and down 4.2% on 2026-11-13 itself (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/540065-why-xtant-medical-holdings-inc8217s-xtnt-stock-is-down-608). The 20-day average volume is about 157k shares, roughly $41k a day, which is extremely thin. AAII reports one analyst downgrade and zero upgrades in the month to 2026-11-12, firm not named. Coverage is BTIG (Buy, $0.60 target, 2026-08-12) and Lucid Capital Markets (Buy, $1 target, initiated 2026-09-02), per Benzinga and Investing.com aggregators.

findings.finding: Through H1 the company booked $43.9m of revenue (Q1 $20.9m, Q2 $23.0m). The FY2026 guide of $99-103m therefore needs H2 of $55.1-59.1m, about $27.5-29.5m a quarter, against a Q2 run-rate of $23.0m. The Q2 10-Q says HEMOBLAST Bellows supply from sole manufacturer Dilon (France) covers expected sales only 'through the end of Q3 2026', is 'uncertain' after that, and Dilon can terminate on 30 days' notice. With Q3 consensus at $25.5-27.1m, Q4 would need about $29-33m, so a second guide cut or a soft Q4 framing on 2026-11-16 is likely. Street FY consensus is still about $102m and Q4 about $30.1m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-11 a 7% revenue miss plus a $2m FY guide trim ($101-105m to $99-103m) gave -28.89% on the day. On 2026-05-13 a guide raise to $101-105m with the HEMOBLAST deal gave -4.0%. Guidance changes have moved this name hard to the downside.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates are not reset. Aggregators still carry FY about $102m and Q4 about $30.1m from 2 analysts, above even the lower guide midpoint, and both analysts rate the stock Buy. If the guide were seen as broken, consensus would sit near or below $97m. Partly priced: the stock is down 41% since the 2026-08-10 close ($0.446 to $0.264) and sits at its 52-week low. The supply caveat lives in a 10-Q risk passage, not in the press release.
findings.independence: The FY guide and H1 figures are in the Q2 and Q1 press releases (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/XTNT/xtant-medical-reports-q2-2026-financial-results; https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1899732/xtant-medical-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results). The Q4 consensus of $30.1m is from https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XTNT/earnings-forecasts. The supply wording is single-source (the 10-Q). Peer biologics softness (separate finding) also points to a guide cut.

findings.finding: Orthobiologics peers that reported after Xtant last spoke had a soft Q3 2026. Alphatec (2026-10-29) said Q3 biologics revenue fell about $1m YoY on lower biologics attachment, cut its FY guide, saw thoracolumbar market growth slow to low single digits, and expects flat biologics into Q4. Bioventus (2026-11-02) cited 'softness in Bone Graft Substitutes', reported elsewhere as about -6%. Orthobiologics were 75% of Xtant's Q2 revenue ($17.4m), and management had promised biologics acceleration in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Biologics shortfall was the stated cause of the 2026-08-11 guide cut (-28.89%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q3 of $25.5-27.1m implies a $2.5-4m sequential step-up. That assumes the promised biologics acceleration plus HEMOBLAST, and it does not reflect peer softness reported 2-3 weeks after the estimates were last set. If priced, Q3 estimates would sit at or below $25m. This is a proxy: Xtant sells through independent agents and has 25 new reps, so its own share gains could offset the market.
findings.independence: Bioventus Q3 release, 2026-11-02: 'softness in Bone Graft Substitutes' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001665988/000166598826000050/bioventusex-991q32026.htm). Globus US spine +2% only (https://finviz.com/news/417606/globus-medical-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-a-500-million-increase-to-the-share-repurchase-program). All are proxies. Net of the rest of the company: spinal implants are about 25% of revenue (~$5.7m), flat-ish after the divestiture, and do not offset.

findings.finding: Liquidity and covenant pressure. At 2026-06-30 the company had $9.9m cash (down from $17.3m at year-end), $23.0m of debt, and only $0.7m available on the revolver. H1 operating cash flow was -$9.4m. MidCap Amendment No. 5 (2026-08-10) waived a Q2 minimum orthobiologics revenue covenant breach, reset the covenant levels (not disclosed), and raised term-loan amortization by $0.15m from Q4 2026 and $0.3m a quarter after that. Q3 is the first test of the reset covenant. The money funds operating losses and the HEMOBLAST sales force, not a corroborated revenue ramp. Management told Canaccord (2026-08-11) it expects to generate cash and need no more capital by Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior print where financing was the surprise. The August print, with a covenant waiver disclosed in the 10-Q, fell 28.9%, but the guide drove that.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market cap is about $37m against $23m of debt, at a 52-week low. What is unpriced is whether Q3 needs another waiver or a raise, or whether the 'cash generation by Q4' claim holds. Neither is visible until the release and 10-Q. If a raise were priced, the stock would have gapped on an 8-K or S-3. EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-11 and no shelf. Financing question answered: the money covers losses under covenant pressure, which is the negative case, so the sign is negative but small.
findings.independence: Management's cash-generation claim cuts the other way (https://quartr.com/events/xtant-medical-holdings-inc-xtnt-canaccord-genuity-s-46th-annual-growth-conference_oSup1xgB). This finding shares the 10-Q document with the guide finding but rests on different numbers (balance sheet and covenant, not revenue run-rate).

findings.finding: HEMOBLAST Bellows changes how it is booked in Q3. In Q2 Xtant acted as agent and booked only $1.3m net of Dilon's fulfilment costs. Management said sales would exceed $1m a month on a GROSS basis as the transition to Xtant contracts completes, and the 10-Q says supply covers sales through the end of Q3. So Q3 headline revenue gets a mechanical lift of about $1.5-2m+ from the switch to gross alone, before any biologics growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first quarter with HEMOBLAST at gross, so there is no history. Revenue beats on this name have been bought: +13.6% on 2025-08-12 and +15.4% on 2025-05-12.
findings.why_not_priced: Probably mostly in the two-analyst consensus, which already steps Q3 up to $25.5-27.1m. The disputed bar caps this finding. If the market had read the gross step-up as a clean beat, the stock would not be making new lows into the print.
findings.independence: The 10-Q gives the agent-versus-principal note and the Q3 supply coverage (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1453593/000149315226036981/form10-q.htm). This is the same HEMOBLAST product as the guide finding, but it points the other way for the reported quarter only. The two are consistent: Q3 gets lifted, Q4 is at risk.

findings.finding: The amnio and skin-substitute headwind cited in the August guide cut has continued. MiMedx (2026-10-28) reported Q3 2026 wound sales down 71% YoY under Medicare's January 2026 flat per-cm2 skin-substitute payment rules. It expects the 2027 framework to be broadly similar, so there is no relief for Xtant's amnio line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Amnio headwinds were a named cause of the 2026-08-11 guide cut (-28.89%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company already named it in the August guide cut, so it lands inside what was guided. Filed small because the peer confirms there was no Q3 recovery.
findings.independence: Finsee review of the MiMedx Q3 (https://finsee.ai/earnings/mdxg/2026/q3/en/) reads the same peer release, so it adds nothing independent.

findings.finding: AAII's data shows one analyst downgraded XTNT and none upgraded in the month to 2026-11-12, with the stock down 66% year to date. On a two-analyst name (BTIG, Lucid), that suggests one estimate set may have been cut before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The firm is unnamed and Benzinga lists no downgrade, so the item is ambiguous. If a firm did downgrade, the bar may already be partly lower, which slightly cuts against the 'estimates not reset' part of the guide finding.
findings.independence: Benzinga's ratings page lists no last downgrade (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XTNT/sentiment), which contradicts this weakly.

outside_window.finding: The Q4 2026 HEMOBLAST supply status and Dilon's 30-day termination right resolve inside the window only if management addresses them on the 2026-11-16 call. Actual Q4 revenue lands in March 2027.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The negative lean agrees with the -9% run-up and the 52-week-low tape, so part of it is already priced. That, plus the disputed bar and the mechanical HEMOBLAST gross lift in Q3, is why p_up is 42 rather than 30.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: $25.5m vs $27.1m from aggregators): the peer-softness finding, which depends on the Q3 revenue bar, capped from -1.5 to -1.0. The HEMOBLAST gross finding was already small at +1.0 and left there. The guide finding is unchanged because it rests on the company's own range.

Rules 4 and 5 (financing is a question; covenant arithmetic has not paid): the liquidity finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0. The financing question was answered: the money covers losses under covenant pressure, so the sign stays negative.
Pessimism artefact plus rule 3 (the caveat that the stock is already at a 52-week low): p_up moved from 40 to 42.

Rule 8 (thin coverage and a likely guidance change): abs_move_pct raised from 13 to 14 (the last print moved -28.9%). The guide finding was left at -3.0 rather than enlarged, because it is arithmetic on primary numbers, not a disclosed number.
Downgrade finding trimmed from -0.3 to -0.2: an unnamed firm, and Benzinga weakly contradicts it.
